glossary.tat: TAT (turnaround time) – time from sample collection to result validation. The median is robust to extreme values.
glossary.pathological: A result outside the reference interval for the patient's sex and age (flag L/H, critical LL/HH).
glossary.critical: A critical value endangers the patient; the laboratory must phone it to the physician immediately.
glossary.samples: Number of unique orders containing at least one result that matches the filters.
glossary.westgard: Westgard rules – a set of statistical rules for evaluating quality-control runs (e.g. 1-3s, 2-2s, R-4s, 10x).
glossary.egfr: eGFR – estimated glomerular filtration rate from creatinine, age and sex (CKD-EPI 2021 equation).
glossary.pointValue: Point value – how many CZK an insurer pays per procedure point. For laboratories it is set by the annual reimbursement decree.
glossary.breakEven: Break-even – the minimum volume at which revenue covers a method's fixed and variable costs.
glossary.histogram: A histogram shows how often values fall into each interval and reveals the shape of the distribution (e.g. skew in enzymes).
glossary.boxplot: A box plot summarises a distribution in five numbers and makes groups easy to compare.
glossary.criticalTarget: Recommended target: phone a critical value to the physician within 30 minutes of validation.
glossary.cv: Coefficient of variation = SD / mean × 100. Measures the imprecision (spread) of repeated control measurements.
glossary.bias: Bias = (control mean − target) / target × 100. Measures systematic deviation of the method.
glossary.leveyJennings: A Levey-Jennings chart plots control measurements over time against the target and ±1, 2 and 3 SD bands.
glossary.percentile: 90th percentile = the value below which 90 % of samples fall. It shows the long tail of slow samples better than the mean.
glossary.ecdf: Empirical cumulative distribution: for each time, the share of samples that already have a result.
glossary.sankey: A Sankey diagram shows flows between states; band width is proportional to the number of results.
glossary.deltaCheck: A delta check compares a result with the same patient's previous result. An unexpectedly large change may indicate a sample mix-up or pre-analytical error.
glossary.pearson: Pearson's r measures a linear relationship (−1 to +1). For skewed data it is computed on logarithms.
glossary.spearman: Spearman's ρ is a rank correlation – robust to outliers and to non-linear (monotonic) relationships.
glossary.r2: The coefficient of determination R² is the share of Y's variance explained by the regression on X.
glossary.mri: Minimum retesting interval (MRI) – the time before which repeating a test usually adds no new information (e.g. HbA1c 90 days).
glossary.costPerResult: Estimate: number of early repeats × actual cost per reportable result of that test from the cost model.
glossary.procedures: A procedure = a reported test result the lab bills to an insurer (points) or to a self-payer.
glossary.absorption: Costs are assigned to reported results: number of results × the method's actual cost per result in that month (absorption costing).
glossary.costPerReportable: Actual cost per reportable result = all method costs (reagents, QC, calibration, expiry, EQA, staff, lease, overhead) / number of reported results.
glossary.pareto: The 80/20 Pareto rule: a small share of items often drives most of the effect. Sorted bars with a cumulative line show how many methods make up 80 %.
glossary.payback: Payback period = one-off introduction costs (validation, training) / monthly operating margin.
glossary.sensitivity: Sensitivity analysis shows which assumptions move the result most. The longest bars are the parameters to verify most carefully.
glossary.makeOrBuy: Make-or-buy compares running a method in-house with sending samples to a reference laboratory. When sent out, the reference lab bills the procedure; we keep only the pre-analytics and transport cost.
glossary.lifecycleLoss: Sum of negative cumulative results of discontinued methods: revenue − all costs including validation, training and expiry.

landing.title: LabInsight
landing.lead: An interactive clinical-laboratory dashboard that answers one question: does this method pay off given its volume and its cost?
landing.clinicalDesc: Results, reference intervals, critical values, quality control and operations.
landing.businessDesc: Points, reimbursement, cost per result, margins, break-even and method lifecycle.
landing.sqlDesc: Your own SQL queries on DuckDB right in the browser.
landing.author: Author

results.pickerHint: Click a bar in the “out of range” chart to switch the test.
results.boxplotSub: Box = 25th–75th percentile, line = median, whiskers = 5th and 95th percentile; groups with n ≥ 20
results.outOfRangeSub: 20 tests with the highest share of abnormal results · click to select a test

critical.timelineSub: Each dot = one critical value; height = time from validation to phone notification
critical.histogramSub: Notifications in 5-minute intervals; those after 30 minutes in orange
critical.byDept: Share reported within 30 min by department

qc.ljSub: Both control levels in SD units from target · default view is the last 90 days; drag the slider to change it
qc.violationsSub: Measurements that would reject the run (newest first)
qc.summarySub: Click a row to show that method's Levey-Jennings chart

tat.heatmapSub: Samples received by weekday and hour
tat.ecdfSub: Share of samples with a result within a given time from collection
tat.phasesSub: Where a sample spends its time · click to filter by priority
tat.sankeySub: Priority → sample condition → outcome (number of results)

patient.gdpr: Patients are pseudonymised: instead of name and national ID only a fictional ID, birth year and district (a GDPR-style approach).
patient.trendSub: Small multiples – each test has its own axis; grey band = reference interval, orange = out of range, red = critical
patient.deltaSub: Results that changed more than usual versus the previous result within {{days}} days

correlation.scatterSub: Values from the same order, random sample of up to {{n}} points, with regression line
correlation.matrixSub: Pearson on logs · blue = negative, red = positive · click a cell to show the pair

ordering.bridge: the bridge between clinic and economics
ordering.profileSub: Share of each requester's orders including the test (15 most frequent) · click to filter the requester
ordering.byTestSub: Share of results repeated before the minimum retesting interval (MRI)
ordering.byDeptSub: Cost = number of early repeats × actual cost per result from the cost model · click to filter

bizOverview.deltaNote: MoM and YoY compare the last month of the period ({{month}}) with the previous month and with the same month last year.
bizOverview.trend: Revenue, costs and margin by month
bizOverview.trendSub: Costs = reported results × actual cost per result from the cost model
bizOverview.byGroup: Revenue, costs and margin by test group

quadrantDesc.stars: high volume and positive margin – the lab's pillars
quadrantDesc.volume: high volume but loss-making – optimise costs
quadrantDesc.cut: low volume and loss-making – consider sending out or discontinuing

frequency.bubbleSub: Bubble size = total revenue · colour = profitability · click to pick a method for the cost curve
frequency.curveSub: Model: fixed costs (QC, calibration, lease, EQA) are spread over fewer results; at low volume reagents also expire
frequency.paretoRevenueSub: {{n}} of {{total}} methods make up 80 % of revenue · click to filter the method
frequency.paretoLossSub: {{n}} of {{total}} loss-making methods make up 80 % of the loss · click to filter
frequency.selectedNote: {{test}}: reagent expiry is {{expiry}} of costs, fixed costs (QC, calibration, EQA, lease, validation) {{fixed}}.

breakeven.formNote: Simulates a single analyser. Revenue = points × point value (self-payers excluded). Staff rates: technician CZK 420/h, specialist CZK 780/h.

verdict.no: Not worth it – the method would lose money

breakeven.verdictText: Break-even is {{be}} results per month; the expected volume of {{freq}} is {{ratio}} of break-even.
breakeven.verdictNever: Even at very high volume revenue never covers costs – revenue per result is below the variable cost.
breakeven.curve: Cost per result vs. revenue per result
breakeven.curveSub: Where the curves cross = break-even; vertical line = expected volume
breakeven.tornadoSub: Change in monthly margin when a parameter moves by ±20 % (base margin {{base}})
breakeven.structureSub: At the expected volume, {{total}} per month in total

makebuy.chartSub: Monthly result of both options by volume · sending out costs {{handling}} per sample (pre-analytics and transport), result in {{tat}} h
makebuy.tableSub: At the actual volume in the period · click a row to chart the method

lifecycle.ganttSub: From introduction to discontinuation · blue successful, red discontinued
lifecycle.planSub: Average results per month · grey plan, coloured actual
lifecycle.cumulativeSub: Revenue − actual costs incl. validation; discontinued methods dashed
lifecycle.lessons: Lessons learned – what should have warned us
lifecycle.planAbove: The plan was {{pct}} above break-even – the decision relied on an optimistic demand estimate.
lifecycle.planBelow: Even the plan was below break-even – the method could never be profitable.
lifecycle.actualBelow: Actual volume reached only {{pct}} of break-even.

payers.kpiPointValueSub: weighted average across insurers and specialties
payers.share: Payers: share of procedures and revenue
payers.trendSub: Monthly revenue stacked by insurer and self-payers
payers.pointValuesSub: Decree No. 432/2025 Coll. × FICTIONAL contract coefficient (simulated individual contracts) · realised = revenue / points
